issues.legal_issue: An alleged land grant by a former sovereign is unenforceable against a successor government that has not accepted it.
material_facts: The claimants sought a declaration of title based on an alleged grant by a former sovereign.
The successor government did not approve the order that purported to recognize the grant.
The order recognizing the alleged grant was held up for review after the former sovereign directed that post-covenant orders be scrutinized.
The appellate courts rejected the oral evidence offered to prove the grant, and the Supreme Court considered the recognition order of limited significance in light of the subsequent order.
The alleged grantee had not entered possession of the lands pursuant to the alleged grant.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming that the grant had been made, it was unenforceable because the successor government had not accepted it. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle in State of Gujarat v. Vora Fiddali Badruddin Mithibarwala that a claim based on a grant by a former sovereign is unenforceable when the successor government has not accepted the grant.

predicates.title_claim_based_on_prior_grant: A claimant brought a proceeding seeking title to land on the basis of an alleged grant by a former sovereign.
predicates.grant_not_accepted_by_successor_governme: The government succeeding the former sovereign did not accept the alleged grant.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks title on the basis of a former sovereign’s grant and the successor government did not accept that grant, the claim based on it is unenforceable.
